Apple has acquired certain assets of SigScalr, the company behind the observability application SigLens, and has hired some of its staff. Here are the details.

Apple acquires part of SigScalr's business

Under the EU's Digital Markets Act, Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta or Microsoft must notify the European Commission when they make acquisitions or other regulated transactions, after which the Commission publishes the details of the deal on its website.

Today, the website was updated with a new Apple acquisition involving SigScalr, the company that develops the observability platform SigLens.

SigLens is an open-source observability platform designed to help developers collect, search, and analyse logs, metrics, and traces generated by applications and infrastructure. SigScalr positioned it as a more efficient alternative to services such as Splunk, Datadog, and Elasticsearch.

Back to the acquisition, here is the statement Apple provided to the EU:

The closing date of the acquisition is listed as 12 March. Since then, SigScalr's official website has been taken offline, and SigLens's main GitHub repository has been archived and set to read-only.

In the archival notice, the developers wrote:

Today, we are officially archiving this project. First and foremost, a huge thank you to all of you. 🙏 What began as a small idea grew, thanks to your involvement, into something far beyond our expectations. Your pull requests, bug reports, feature suggestions, stars, blog posts, tweets, and every word of encouragement made this project what it is. The trust you placed in us, and the time you gave, mean the world to us.

What do you think Apple will do with this acquisition? Let us know in the comments.
